_readme: Who grants a bonded creature, as data rather than a hard-coded class check (D6, ticket #30).
Consumed by utils/class_func/animal_companions.py::resolve_bonded_creatures, which is the
SINGLE path to a bonded creature. Gated by scripts/validate_companion_data.py (vocabulary).
Columns:
grantor          class name, or a non-class source identified by `source`
creature_type    companion | mount | familiar | eidolon
level_gained     the grantor's own class level at which the creature arrives; below this,
NOTHING is emitted -- there is no clamp to level 1 (D6)
effective_level  an expression over `level` (the grantor's OWN class level, never the
character level and never the total of all classes). Stacked across
sources, then capped at character level.
minimum          a per-source floor applied AFTER the expression. Only Beastmastery has one,
and it is RAW from the talent's own text -- not the clamp D6 rejects.
conditional      what else must be true (e.g. the rolled sorcerer bloodline)
species_pool     which animal_choices.json tiers, or a named creature list
choice           {odds, on_win, on_loss} when the class feature is a choice. The resolver
draws random.randint(1, 100) ONCE PER ROW -- never reusing domain_chance,
whose single roll used to make the druid's two outcomes mutually exclusive
by construction.
Not rows, and deliberately (#23): `shifter` (its progression contains no animal companion),
`antipaladin` (Fiendish Boon is a permanent summon monster III+, a different subsystem --
deferred), and unconditional `sorcerer` (Arcane Bond comes from the Arcane bloodline only).
`magical_beast` is absent from every standard pool on purpose: griffon and hippogriff are
reachable only through an archetype's curated species_pool.
